### Session 198-PRE — 2026-08-04 — **THE HOMEPAGE HAD BEEN ADVERTISING APRIL ARTICLES AS NEW SINCE MAY, THE SEARCH PAGE SHIPPED 10.4 MB TO EVERY PHONE, AND THE SITE'S MOST ABSOLUTE LAW HAD NOTHING ENFORCING IT** — six diagnostic passes run at Aaron's request *before* S198 opened, every finding sitting underneath a green gate, and not one of them findable by reading a file

**THE FINDING THAT NAMES THE OTHERS: every defect lived in the gap between what a file SAYS and what a reader RECEIVES.** The gate was green at 15 checks when this began and green at 18 when it ended; nothing in between was visible to grep, to a validator, or to reasoning. The manifest needed a browser (its hrefs did not exist until JavaScript built them). The 9.4 MB payload needed a network measurement (the markup was valid and the file was named in no rule). The two mobile defects needed a 390px viewport and a *distrust of `scrollWidth`*, which `body { overflow-x: hidden }` had been quietly falsifying at every width for months. **Full forensic record: `archive/S198-PRE-SESSION-AUDIT.md`.**

**§A — THE HOMEPAGE'S THREE DISCOVERY DOORS, DEAD SINCE APRIL.** `content-manifest.js` last generated 2026-05-27, newest entry dated **2026-04-04**. It powers Spotlight, Discover Random, and Recently Added — **and only those three.** Pool was 533 against 611 canonical prose pages: **127 pages, 20% of the corpus including every `analytical-*` page, unreachable through any of the three.** Cause, and it is the lesson: `generate-manifest.js` derived dates by shelling out to `git log`, GIT POLICY reads ZERO EXCEPTIONS, **so no session would run it and the artifact rotted silently.** Rewritten git-free; dates now live **write-once** in `archive/manifest-dates.json` (533 recovered from the old manifest, 115 stamped from each page's own JSON-LD `datePublished`, so homepage and structured data cannot contradict each other); mtime deliberately unused. **533 → 606 entries, 0 dead URLs.** Now the **eighth** pipeline script, after `build-search-index.js`. **New law in CLAUDE.md: a build script no session is willing to run is a stale artifact with extra steps — if a tool conflicts with a standing policy, the conflict is the bug.**

**§B — THE EMOJI BAN, ENFORCED FOR THE FIRST TIME (CHECK 16).** The word "emoji" appeared in `validate-site.js` **zero times** — the most absolute rule on the site was the only major law with nothing behind it. Two survivors. `global.css` carried `✕` (U+2715) in a `content:` property, painting into every row of the cannot-list on `question-dead-man-visual`. And **`search.html` carried `&#128270;` — a magnifying glass as a decimal HTML entity, pure ASCII in the source**, which every codepoint sweep the site has ever run, S74's included, walked straight past; it sat in the no-results state, i.e. on the screen of every reader who searched and did not find. CHECK 16 decodes **four** forms (literal, CSS escape, HTML entity hex+decimal, JS escape) — and it does so only because **the first draft caught `✨` and waved through `content: "\2728"` on the very next line.** That miss is why `search.html` was found at all. Arrows (U+2190–U+21FF) deliberately not banned; `→` is typography.

**§C — THE SEARCH PAGE WAS FIFTY TIMES HEAVIER THAN THE FRONT DOOR.** Measured at 390px: `/search.html` **10.41 MB** against the homepage's 0.21 MB. 9.44 MB of it was `search-index.js` — the full body text of 683 pages — **render-blocking, no `defer`.** Now fetched on demand by `ensureIndex()`, a three-state loader every entry point funnels through. **The whole fix is one subtlety:** the warm-up listeners bind **on the next tick**, because the input carries `autofocus`, which fires during load — the first implementation bound immediately and measured no better than before. **Lands without searching: 10.41 MB → 0.97 MB.** Search quality unchanged; verified across cold load, typing, topic pill, and `?q=` deep link.

**§D — CHECK 12 WAS AN ALLOWLIST WEARING A BUDGET'S CLOTHES.** It named three files — the three that happened to be a problem in S194 — so 9.4 MB was structurally invisible to it and it printed green over that page every session since. **Rewritten as a size budget, deny-by-default: any script over 100 KB must `defer`, whatever it is called, forever.** Proven to fail first. **General form, now canon: a guard that enumerates known offenders only ever catches the past. Enumerate the condition, not the instances.** It nearly broke search on the way out — the dynamic `s.src =` made the index vanish from CHECK 7's runtime set, and **CHECK 7 printed the exact `410!` line that would have taken site search offline.** Widened to match `.src =`, `import()` and `fetch()`. *A check that recommends a fix must be right about what the fix does.*

**§E — NOBODY HAD EVER TESTED A PHONE.** Every render check the site owned measured 1196px and 1600px. `psychology-why-we-resist` carried `white-space: nowrap` on `.pairing-scripture`, whose **15 live uses across 3 pages all hold real prose (73–748 chars)** — whole Scripture quotations on one unbreakable line **3,182px wide**; on a 390px phone the reader saw **12% of Romans 1:18** with no way to know the rest existed, and it was broken at *every* width. `the-golden-chain` had **432px of its closing call-to-action off-screen** (a grid inside a flex parent; `min-width: auto` refuses to shrink below a min-content of 782px). Both fixed. `the-mirror`'s 8px is deliberate full-bleed and correctly left alone. **New standing tool `archive/s198-mobile-check.js`** walks element rects rather than trusting `scrollWidth`; 390 and 768 are now law (CLAUDE.md PRESENTATION INTEGRITY §8).

**§F — THE SCRIPTURE CHECKER HAD BEEN TRIANGULATING AROUND GROUND TRUTH SITTING IN THE REPO (CHECK 17).** `verify-scripture.js` compared the site's quotations **against each other**, its own header explaining it worked *"without needing a licensed Bible text to diff against"* — a premise obsolete for as long as `scripture-niv.js` (992 NIV passages, already served to every reader) had existed. Cost: it could only say *"these two differ,"* never *"this one is wrong,"* so nobody ever worked its 269 findings — and **it was structurally blind to the worst case, a verse misquoted the SAME way on every page, which looks like perfect consistency.** That is exactly what it was hiding. **Exodus 33:19, a Romans 9 keystone, was quoted with a word dropped** — "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy" for "…on whom I *will* have mercy." **1 Timothy 6:10 read "*the* root of all kinds of evil" in an `<h3>` on `word-study-every-all`** — a page whose entire subject is people over-reading a word — while the blockquote three lines below had it right. **Amos 3:2 was the most instructive:** the page quoted "You only have I *known*" (KJV/ESV) to argue *yada* means covenantal love, when the NIV renders it **"chosen"** — the reader's own Bible made the page's point better than the page did. Rewritten per §XV. Seven fixed by hand. **2,638 VERIFIED · 203 MISQUOTE · 84 HEADING · 350 UNMATCHED.** Three classifications were earned by my own false positives (ellipsis must survive normalization; the NIV source has verse numbers and section headings glued in; **a title-case string near a reference is a heading — "God Commands All to Repent" sat beside Acts 17:30 on nine pages at 100% word overlap**). CHECK 17 ceiling **203**, ratchet-only. **Queue: `archive/S198-scripture-queue.txt`, 192 distinct, sorted by edit distance — 45 one word off, 52 two-or-three, 45 short rewrites, 50 compressions.** That last category is theological work and must not be automated: *a compressed verse inside quotation marks is not a typo; it is the page quietly improving on Scripture.*

**§G — 26 DOORWAYS FAILED WCAG 2.4.1, AND THE REPAIR SCRIPT HELD A LOADED GUN.** Accessibility had never been swept and is otherwise strong (zero missing `alt`, exactly one `<h1>` on 686 pages, `lang` everywhere, all 670 in-page anchors resolving). But **26 pages had no skip link and the list was the worst possible one** — `questions`, `start-here`, `topics`, every hub, and **every audience landing page including `for-hurting` and `for-doubters`.** `fix-skip-links.js` had been bailing on them for want of an `<article class="article-body">` wrapper, though 22 use `.hub-container` and the rest have a `<main>`. **686/686 now covered, all links resolving.** While in there: **the script still wrote `id` BEFORE `class`** — the exact literal-string trap that took the article count from 618 to 89 in S194. It reported "0 pages" and looked harmless only because every article page already had a link; **the first new one without would have silently deleted itself from all 21 consumers.** Fixed and proven.

**§H — THE STALE DATES, DELIBERATELY NOT BULK-FIXED.** 373 pages still claim `dateModified: 2026-04`, 228 article pages carry none at all, and nothing has a `datePublished` past 2026-06-30. **Not auto-corrected, and the reason is the law itself:** there is no honest record of when each page changed — git history is off-limits, `coverage.json` holds session numbers without dates, mtime is meaningless because the pipeline rewrites everything every run. Stamping 373 pages with today's date tells every crawler the corpus changed in one day: untrue, and a spam signal. **The existing error understates freshness; the invented one would overstate it, which is the direction that deceives.** `stamp-modified.js` (new, `--check` for the distribution) makes the field a record going forward; the 12 pages touched here are stamped. S198 decides separately about the historical 373, knowing no honest signal exists to reconstruct them.

**§I — FIFTH PASS: THE STRUCTURED DATA HAD NEVER ONCE BEEN PARSED (CHECK 18).** Aaron asked the question a third time; the sweep went at the laws themselves — *which of this site's absolute rules have anything enforcing them* — plus the angles four passes had not touched. **`ot-joseph.html` shipped invalid JSON-LD.** An FAQPage answer quoted Acts 4:28 inside a JSON string with the quotation marks left raw — `did what God's "power and will had decided beforehand should happen."` — which voids **the entire block**: Google discards the whole FAQ, no error surfaces anywhere, and the surrounding HTML is flawless, so CHECK 1 and CHECK 3 both walk past. **The same blindness class as the manifest and the payload, for the third time: the file was fine; what the recipient received was not.** Fixed with single quotes rather than backslash escapes, so the next editor cannot reintroduce it as easily. **CHECK 18** parses every `ld+json` block on all 687 pages — zero tolerance, not a ratchet, because malformed JSON is never a judgement call. Proven to fail first on `objection-love.html`. **The clone ceiling is therefore CHECK 19.**

**And the honest half of that pass: most of what it went looking for was already clean.** `TL;DR` as visible text: **zero** (the 631 hits were a `class="tldr"` on a box that renders *In Brief* — left for S198, since `.tldr` must be grepped against all 21 literal-string consumers first). Banned in-page TOC (`.section-nav` / `.article-toc`): **zero**. `(NIV)` appended after quotations: **zero**. Mixed content, mojibake, BOMs: **zero**. Duplicate `<title>` and duplicate meta descriptions across 687 pages: **zero of each**, and 686/687 carry a description. `robots.txt` correct and pointing at the sitemap; **685 sitemap entries, none dead**; every internal href in `nav.js` resolves. The six odd-hour matches were read by hand and **none is the banned manufactured-crisis scene** — a hymn sung at full volume in the night, soldiers at the door in the Korean persecution, 7:14 a.m. and 9:22 a.m. on a printable. The seven `sinful nature` hits are Romans 7:18 (which the 2011 NIV does render that way) or the site's own prose, not the banned 1984 Romans 8:8 reading. **A sweep that reports everything it touched as broken is not reading, it is flattering itself.**

**§J — SIXTH PASS: 440 PAGES SKIPPED A HEADING LEVEL, AND THE CAUSE WAS ONE ACCIDENTAL CSS SELECTOR.** Aaron asked a fourth time. **440 of 687 pages had a broken document outline** — h2 straight to h4 — and on **395 the skip was in exactly one place: the footer's column headings.** A screen-reader user navigating by heading level hears a level vanish, on 64% of the corpus, invisible to all eighteen checks. `fix-heading-hierarchy.js` promotes footer `<h4>` to `<h3>`, **with a guard that is the whole reason it is not a one-line sed**: 29 pages carry an `<h3>` *inside* the footer with the columns nested beneath it, where the outline already reads h2→h3→h4 correctly and promoting would DESTROY a level rather than restore one. 582 pages, 1,821 headings. Remaining skips: 45, all body-level, **deliberately not automated** — each is a judgement about what a heading means, and a script that guesses is renumbering an argument's structure. `--report` lists them.

**And underneath it, an older accident that had been quietly overriding the footer's own design.** `[class*="section"] h4` (~line 3209) matches `.footer-section`, and being later in the file at equal specificity it beat `.footer-section h4` for as long as both existed — rendering every footer in Inter 1.1rem/600 instead of the Playfair 1.05rem/700 with the ember underline the stylesheet actually asks for. So the tag promotion *silently restored the intended design*, which is a site-wide visual change smuggled in under an accessibility fix. It is now explicit and uniform: a specificity-boosted rule gives the 29 surviving `<h4>` footers the same treatment, so every footer on the site renders identically and as written.

**Three tool failures on the way, and the middle one is the lesson.** The first render harness loaded pages over `file://`. Every page links `/global.css` — root-absolute — which under `file://` resolves to the filesystem root, 404s in silence, and leaves you measuring **Chrome's UA stylesheet**. It reported a confident 16px → 18.72px "regression" across five archetypes. Those are the UA defaults to the decimal: h4 is 1em, h3 is 1.17em. **A tool that has never been checked against a known-good case is not evidence** — the harness now refuses to report unless `getComputedStyle(body).backgroundColor` proves the site stylesheet loaded, and it serves over HTTP. The second: three of the five sample pages were *guarded* pages the script had correctly skipped, so the "before" variant was a file that never existed. The third: the CSS edit was chained behind a `cp` backup that failed on the read-only mount, so **570 pages shipped with headings whose selectors had not been updated** — caught only because the verification step was run anyway. *Chaining a repair behind a convenience command means the convenience decides whether the repair happens.* **Verified by screenshot, not inference**: footer renders correctly at 1196px and 390px, Playfair loaded, zero overflowing elements.

**Also swept clean in the sixth pass:** every one of **8,481 static asset references resolves** — no missing `og-image.png`, favicon, manifest, or stylesheet anywhere. `_redirects` audited whole for the first time: **203 rules, zero pointing at a nonexistent target, zero duplicate sources, zero chains.** `_headers` carries CSP, HSTS, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `nosniff` and a locked-down `Permissions-Policy`. `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured in five places against 15 keyframe animations. *(The 25 rules that first read as "non-forced and shadowed by a real file" are `/foo → /foo.html [200]` extensionless rewrites — the tool was counting `foo.html` as proof that `/foo` exists. Same lesson as the manifest, one layer down.)*

**Smaller.** Three root PDFs — `Jesus' Path to Eternal Life`, `The Institutes Book 3 essay`, `The_Question_of_the_Hour` — are on `PUBLIC_EXACT`, absent from the sitemap, and **linked from nowhere.** Checked for the `RE-FORMED.pdf` failure mode and **clean**: no real name in text or metadata (`/Author` reads `Un-named` / `(anonymous)`). Dead weight, not exposure — wire them in or 410 them. **132 titles exceed 65 characters** and truncate in search results, which matters for the 90-second searcher the benchmarking report names as gap #1. `_headers` carried a cache rule for `/search-index.json`, **a file that has never existed on this site** — the real asset fell through to the generic `/*.js` rule, which now matters at 9.4 MB on demand. All 113 linked Reformed Sources PDFs resolve, `%20` intact, zero broken. CHECK 7 caught the new `stamp-modified.js` immediately and printed its own `410!` line, added same session.

**Carries forward, unchanged from S197.** The clone ceiling — **271 passages / 4,944 duplicated words — is still owed, and it is now CHECK 18, not 16** (16 and 17 are taken). Gospel-absence queue at 134 with 3 worked. **The 21 scripts keyed to the brittle `<article class="article-body">` literal remain the oldest open item.** 167 pages carry a lock with no session tag. CHECK 10 at 724/235.

**Pipeline** GREEN, full **eight**-script run (manifest restored to it). **ALL 18 CHECKS PASSED** · desktop render clean at 1196/1600 with Playfair confirmed loaded · **mobile render clean at 390/768** across all six archetypes · `canonical-conformance` 686/686 · `fix-orphaned-cards` and `fix-stray-progress-bar` dry-runs inert · manifest current at 606 · every root `.md` and `.js` carries its forced `410!` · `tags.json`, `/all-content` and the homepage all agree at **611**.

### Session 197 — 2026-08-04 — **ONE DEPRAVITY PARAGRAPH HAD BEEN PASTED ONTO ELEVEN PAGES, AND THE DETECTOR BUILT TO FIND EXACTLY THAT HAD BEEN RUNNING GREEN FOR SIXTEEN SESSIONS** — because its default threshold could not see a two-page clone and its output buried the signal under 1,110 rows of Ephesians 1:4

**THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE ONE THE SITE'S DEEPEST LAW EXISTS TO PREVENT.** The P0 cold read found what the law predicted — but not on one page. `theologian-owen` and `shattered-lens-taught-wrong`, both shipped in S196, closed with the same sentence: *"The way to find out whether you are among the given is not to [audit yourself / search your interior] for evidence. It is to come — and discover that you were brought."* And `devotional-you-were-wanted-before-you-were` and `shattered-lens-taught-wrong` both covered the numb reader with the identical clause, *"nothing has gone wrong and nothing has been withheld."* **Three pages, one night, two signature sentences.** That is §XVIII.3 exactly — *"if an agent reading the page can feel the checklist through the prose, the page has failed even with every box ticked"* — and §XI.20's fingerprint test, failed against the previous session's own output.

**Pulling that thread found something an order of magnitude larger.** `detect-shared-phrases.js` has existed since S181 for precisely this. Run as shipped it reported **1,110 hits, and the top of the list was 68 pages sharing "chose you before the foundation of the world."** That is not a clone; that is the site's doctrine in Paul's words, which it should say on every page it can. Three design faults, each alone enough to make the report unreadable — **and an unreadable report is not a check**:

1. **The threshold was the selector.** Default `--min 3` is structurally incapable of seeing a two-page clone, and a two-page clone *is* the defect. Default is now **2**.
2. **It reported shingles, not passages.** One cloned paragraph surfaced as a dozen overlapping n-grams each with its own page list, so ~40 real findings wore 1,053 rows. Seeds are now **extended maximally in both directions while every occurrence still agrees**, then deduplicated — one row per cloned passage.
3. **Scripture escaped the strip whenever it was unquoted.** The quote-span strip only catches verses inside quotation marks; allusion and running paraphrase sail through, which is what put Ephesians 1:4 and Philippians 1:6 at the head of the list. Every candidate is now checked against `scripture-niv.js` and dropped if the NIV contains it. Ranking is by **duplicated volume** — words × extra pages, the number of words a reader going door to door meets a second time.

**Rebuilt, it printed the real thing on the first run.** A single depravity module — *"He means you hate holiness… your nature recoils from the righteousness of God the way your hand recoils from a flame… You find ten minutes of prayer exhausting but can scroll your phone for two hours without effort… you can muster genuine emotion watching a movie but sit stone-cold through a sermon about the cross… a death no human willpower can reverse, because the will itself is the thing that's dead"* — **verbatim across ELEVEN pages**, six of them carrying five or six of its fragments each, and the *scaffold sentence in front of it* (*"Here is the problem with the corpse metaphor: you are clearly alive…"*) transplanted with it, with only the noun swapped (`analogy-adoption` says "orphan metaphor"). **26 pages carry at least one fragment.** §XIII.2 names this in one line — *"the same angle in identical phrasing across articles is the slogan-trap"* — and §XXI names its victim: the reader who stays, who reads ten pages tonight, and meets the same mirror seven times.

**§A — FIFTEEN PAGES DE-CLONED, EACH GIVEN A DIFFERENT ANGLE OFF THE §XIII.2 BENCH, DERIVED FROM THE PAGE'S OWN IMAGE.** No page got a stock replacement; the craft law is that the mirror has to grow out of what the page is already about.
- **`analogy-adoption`** — the biggest lift and the one piece of new ground: *"He means the orphan does not want the home."* A child institutionalised long enough does not experience the arrival of a family as rescue but as **threat** — the ward is terrible and the ward is *known*, and a house with a garden is the loss of every skill he has. *"Ask him and he will tell you, in perfect sincerity, that he would rather stay."* The catch then lands inside the same image: the will *"has to be replaced and not persuaded, because the wanting is precisely what the ward took."*
- **`question-what-is-sovereign-grace`** — five paragraphs of transplanted mirror replaced by two of **Augustine's two volitions**, native to a definitional page: *"You can change what you do about a desire whenever you like; you have never once changed a desire by deciding to."* 290 words → 200.
- **`psychology-anosognosia-of-sin`** keeps the "you don't even know you hate it" material (that clause *is* anosognosia) and gets the **good-day test** plus the clinical tell: *"Notice that you had a reason ready before the question finished. So does every patient asked to lift the arm… What the examiner is listening for was never the content of the excuse. It was the speed."*
- **`anxious-mind-what-if-not-chosen`** — the **Romans 7** mirror, and **a live §XXIII feeling-slip removed on the worst possible page for one**: it closed *"if you do want God right now, something has happened to you that you did not do to yourself"* — a conditional catch handing a self-grading instrument to a reader whose entire fear is that he is not chosen. Now refused out loud (§XXIII.3 move 3): *"the question that has been keeping you up — do I want Him enough for it to count? — is the one question Scripture never once puts to you. It asks who raised Lazarus."*
- **`question-is-salvation-my-choice-or-gods`** — the caused-preference regress, closed with a hostile witness: *"A man is free to do as he wills; he has never once been free to will as he wills. The sentence is Schopenhauer's, and he was no friend of ours when he wrote it."* **`question-chosen`** — thirty seconds of unedited interior monologue. **`question-depravity`, `analogy-doctor-corpse`, `secular-billion-decisions`, `systematic-pneumatology`, `creed-canons-dort`, `question-why-does-god-choose-some-not-others`** — five by subtraction plus one new mirror each (the eleven-years-of-Mondays patient; the moralised vocabulary the flesh reaches for when a sermon convicts; the infant who was never taught to say *mine*).
- **A SECOND transplanted module surfaced the moment the first cleared** — *"spiritual death means you love what God hates… you can binge an entire television series in one sitting but have never once binged Scripture"* on four pages, two sharing 100 words verbatim. `question-dead-in-sin-meaning` keeps it; `analogy-drowning-man`, `systematic-hamartiology` and `question-freewill` were given their own.
- **Result: duplicated volume 7,339 → 4,944 words (−33%), and every cloned *paragraph* is gone from the top of the report.** What remains at the head is the golden chain's own verb list (*foreknown, predestined, called, justified, glorified*), which is Scripture repeating itself and is supposed to.

**§B — THE REST OF THE P0 COLD READ.** `theologian-owen`: the borrowed closer replaced by the page's own opening scene (Move 10) — *"He did not first establish that he was among the given and then walk to Aldermanbury. He went out to hear somebody else, sat down under a stranger whose name is lost, and found out on the way home."* Also **"Two Gospel writers, one conclusion" — Acts is not a Gospel** (now "Christ in the Gospel and Luke in the Acts"); the **label H2 "The Three Doors"** replaced (§I.3), which also cleared a corpus collision with `reformed-apologetics-moral-argument`'s "three doors out, each locked from the inside" — Owen's page now runs on its own clamp; a **weak verse-collage clincher cut** (Mark 10:45's "ransom for many" plus Matthew 25:46 proved nothing the substitution logic above it had not already proved, and *rabbim* is exactly where a sharp opponent enters); and "declining academic posts from **English bishops**" corrected — bishops do not offer academic posts.

**§C — THE DEFERRED COMPRESSION JUDGMENT, DECIDED: NO MOVE LEAVES.** `reformed-apologetics-moral-argument` stays at ~3,650 words against a 2,024–3,273 sibling range, and the overage is **ruled legitimate rather than paid**. The page carries the complete objection space — error theory, relativism, non-naturalist robust realism, Street's dilemma, the noetic-suppression cost, third-factor accounts, Euthyphro, the second-order Euthyphro, the forgiveness asymmetry — and §XXII.1's capacities 1 and 6 (*exhaustive engagement*, *total escape-route closure*) cost words. A 2,024-word sibling on a narrower topic is not evidence this page is long; it is evidence the topics differ in size. The "I can be good without God" paragraph is 60 words and closes the single most common objection an actual atheist voices — cutting it to hit a number would open an exit the standard requires welded. **What was actually owed was measured instead: 19 antithesis constructions across 34 paragraphs** (§XXII.4's named tell — *"once is a hammer; every third paragraph is a machine"*), **and three consecutive paragraphs of 199 / 151 / 211 words at the page's climax**, which is where the reader is asked to do the hardest work and given the least air. Both fixed: the two longest split at their natural seams, three tic-antitheses removed.

**§D — GOSPEL-ABSENCE, WORKED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN FOUR SESSIONS — AND ONE PAGE'S CATCH WAS CONTRADICTING TOTAL DEPRAVITY.** `secular-genetics-sovereignty` ended: *"you were always meant to be loved by God, and **you were created capable of receiving that love**"* — the exact fruit-gate failure §XVII.4 exists to kill, on a page with **zero** mentions of the cross. Rebuilt out of the page's own image: the genome you did not write, Adam's inheritance you did not vote on, *"if a man can be ruined by a head he never chose, he can be rescued by one,"* closing *"You did not write the code you were born with, and you did not write the one you were born again with. Justified is not… **The chain is unbreakable because one of its links is a body.**"* And `presuppositional-impossibility-of-the-contrary` was checked and **cleared as a false positive** — its catch names *"the loud and bleeding center of history, the Logos made flesh"*; the detector scored it 1 because of its selector, not its content. *A detector's silence is only as wide as its selector — and so is its noise.*

**§E — THE UNDER-LINKED QUEUE IS EMPTY FOR THE FIRST TIME.** All 18 remaining pages raised to **11–13** verified prose links (**+81 links, 0 broken, 0 duplicates**), worked by two bounded subagents against `archive/s196-page-inventory.txt` under the rule that every href appear in it verbatim; both survived. Every addition cross-category. Independently re-verified after: 18/18 structurally intact, zero broken hrefs, CHECK 11 clean. **Two bugs found in the tool that generates the queue:** `archive/s196-count-prose-links.js` had **S196's sandbox mount path hardcoded** (`/sessions/lucid-amazing-clarke/...`) and threw EACCES on first use in any later session; and **it never wrote the file the S197 kickoff said it writes** — it only prints. So `archive/s196-underlinked-queue.txt` on disk was S196's *pre*-repair snapshot, showing 28 pages that had already been fixed. Path now resolves from `__dirname`; output captured to `archive/s197-underlinked-queue.txt`.

**§F — Also fixed:** `apologetic-he-bore-the-sin-of-many` presented Isaiah 53:5 in quotation marks as *"pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities"* — **two silent deletions inside a quoted verse** (§V.2), on a site that welds the translation hatch shut by never touching the text. ### Session 196 — 2026-08-03 — **A REGEX IN THE BUILD PIPELINE HAD BEEN QUIETLY EATING THE SITE'S OWN DOORWAYS**, and the identical regex in the validator was reporting the damage as noise — plus the render check owed since S195 finally ran, in-sandbox, and immediately found a gold band painted across 104 pages

**THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE FIRST ONE IN MANY SESSIONS THAT WAS ACTIVELY GETTING WORSE ON EVERY RUN.** `dedupe-prose-links.js` masks card decks so their links are neither counted nor stripped. The mask was `/<(?:div|nav|…)[^>]*class="[^"]*(?:keep-reading|…)[^"]*"[\s\S]*?<\/(?:div|nav|…)>/gi`. **The `[\s\S]*?` is non-greedy, so the mask ended at the first closing tag inside the deck — `<div class="card-number">01</div>`.** Measured on `devotional-you-were-wanted-before-you-were`: the mask covered **185 bytes of a 1,582-byte deck. Twelve percent.** Cards 02 and 03 were never protected at all.

So on any page whose deck pointed at a target the prose above had already linked, the deck's own `<a>` wrapper was "de-duplicated" — stripped, leaving the card's title and description sitting in the grid as **unclickable text beside working cards.** A doorway rendering as a dead end. **41 orphaned cards across 21 pages**, accumulating a little more every time the pipeline ran. CHECK 1 was structurally incapable of seeing it: it asks whether links *resolve*, and there was no longer a link to resolve.

**And the same regex, character for character, was in `validate-site.js` CHECK 11** — where it produced the opposite symptom: deck cards counted as prose, **25 pages reported as duplicate-link offenders that were not offenders.** One bug, two inverted symptoms, and the validator's false-positive noise is exactly what would have made a real report look routine. Both are now a real **tag-balance walker** (nested HTML is not a regular language), plus a second independent guard in the linker that refuses to unwrap any anchor containing card markup. `fix-orphaned-cards.js` recovers each lost `href` in strict order — the page's *own* archived backup first (two pages carry cards titled "Perseverance of the Saints" pointing at *different* targets), then a global title index, then four resolved by hand; anything unresolvable is **reported and left alone**, because a wrong link is worse than a visibly missing one. **CHECK 11 was verified by injecting a real duplicate, watching it fail, and restoring** (PRESENTATION INTEGRITY law 3).

**§A — THE RENDER CHECK RAN. It was owed since S195 and it found something on its first execution.** S195 wrote CLAUDE.md law 5 and could not obey it: the sandbox is arm64 and Puppeteer's bundled Chrome is x86-64. **Playwright ships an arm64 Linux Chromium**; with one missing shared library pulled via `apt-get download libxdamage1` (no root needed), `archive/s196-render-check.js` now serves the repo over local HTTP and drives a real browser **against the working tree, not the deployed site** — which matters, since the deploy always lags the session doing the checking. Two results, both instructive:
- **The "nav wrapped to 2 rows" failure was the detector, not the site.** The wordmark is vertically centred in the 51px bar (top=12); the nav links are full-height (top=0). Measured, not reasoned about; the detector now excludes the wordmark. **The nav is fine at 1196px and 1600px.**
- **The gold band was real. `<div class="progress-bar"></div>` — bare, empty, a direct child of `<body>` — on 104 pages.** It looks like a reading bar. It is not: `.reading-progress` (the real one) is `position: fixed`, 2px, scroll-driven; **`.progress-bar` is the quiz/statistics track — 8px, gold-tinted, and with no `position` at all.** So it rendered in normal flow. Measured at 1196px: **1196 × 8px at top=63**, a full-width empty band wedged between the fixed nav and the hero, permanently at 0% because nothing drives it, on the first screen the reader ever sees. Fifteen static checks passed on all 104 pages, because the HTML is valid, the class exists, and the CSS rule exists. The defect lived in the gap between the class the markup asked for and the rule it resolves to. Swept by `fix-stray-progress-bar.js` (empty form only; the 9 pages using `.progress-bar` for its actual purpose are untouched). The check now fails on **any empty element painting a visible band in normal flow** — the general form of the defect, not the instance.

**§B — THE P0 COLD READ: THREE OF THREE PAGES S195 SHIPPED UNREAD FAILED. The law is now four-for-four.** (S193→2 of 4, S194→5 of 5, S195→3 of 3.)

### Session 195 — 2026-08-02 — **ALL FIVE PAGES S194 REBUILT FAILED THE COLD READ — AND THE TWO WORST DEFECTS WERE A GREEK CLAIM THAT IS NOT IN THE GREEK AND A NIV QUOTATION THAT IS NOT IN THE NIV.** Plus: 618 pages had been shipping their own audit vocabulary into public view-source

**THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE KICKOFF'S LAW PROVEN HARDER.** S194 read the four pages S193 shipped unread; two failed. S195 read the five pages S194 shipped unread: **five of five failed.** The law is now unambiguous — *a repair session verifies facts and structure and has no instrument for checking whether the argument it just wrote survives the strongest opponent, or whether the warrant it just invented is really in the text.* Two of this session's five were not craft failures but **integrity** failures, the kind the site's whole credibility rests on:

- **`devotional-you-were-wanted-before-you-were` welded its new section onto a Greek word that is not there.** The page claimed *lavished* in Ephesians 1:8 is *"that word again — the one John reaches for in his letter"* (1 John 3:1). It is not. Eph 1:8 is **ἐπερίσσευσεν** (*eperisseusen*, περισσεύω, to overflow); 1 John 3:1 is **δέδωκεν** (*dedōken*, δίδωμι, has given), and the NIV's "lavished" there is an amplification carrying **ποταπήν**. The weld was an English-only pun — and **NIV-only**: ESV, NASB, KJV, CSB and NRSV all read "has given," so a reader opening any second Bible finds the argument gone. §XV.5 in its purest failure mode, on a site whose entire NIV policy exists so *open your own Bible and read it* works. **The honest repair is stronger and shipped:** rebuilt on *eperisseusen* itself, which is not a word for generosity but for **surplus** — the same form Paul uses at Romans 5:15 (grace *overflowing* through the one man), and the word the Gospels use for **the twelve basketfuls picked up off the grass after five thousand men had eaten their fill.** *"That is the accounting on the blood. Not a sum that barely covered it. Baskets left over."* Same page also claimed of Christ *"who has not once asked to be released from it"* — **Gethsemane**, three times, Luke 22:42 — now *"who asked once in a garden whether the cup could pass, and then drank it to the bottom."* Close 4 beats → 1, landing *"Sit down. There is more than enough."* Links 3 → 11.
- **`shattered-lens-taught-wrong` had Hebrews 4:12 as *"sharper than any two-edged sword."*** NIV 2011 reads **"double-edged."** Four other live pages have it right; this one had been wrong through S183, S186, S193 and S194. The hardest guardrail on the site, broken on a page four consecutive sessions had scanned.

**§A — `theologian-owen`: THE TRILEMMA'S FIRST DOOR WAS A STRAWMAN.** *"Choose first that Christ died for all the sins of all people. Then no one perishes — universalism."* No Arminian grants that inference, because none holds the atonement is *applied* apart from faith; the page defeated a position nobody occupies, and the reader §XIX exists for closes the tab there. The objector now states his own case at full strength (*sufficient for all, efficient for those who believe*) and is answered with **Owen's own hinge, which the page had omitted entirely** — *"But this unbelief, is it a sin, or is it not? If it be, then Christ died for it; if He did, why must that hinder them more than their other sins for which He died?"* Also: *"the centuries since have not produced a single answer"* (live in the body **and three meta carriers**) is false — Baxter answered inside Owen's lifetime — now *"no answer has yet come back that does not, at the last step, hand the deciding vote to the corpse."* Vice-Chancellorship went **1657**, deanery **1660** (the page had both falling in 1660); the deathbed line to Payne restored to *"that glory… or was capable of doing in this world"*; the seam left by S194's deleted pivot sentence closed by making the pronoun carry it (*"The grip in that sentence was never Owen's"*) rather than re-announcing the turn; the `Soli Deo Gloria` tag cut (the footer repeats it three inches below) so the real final line stands alone: **"He is not going to begin with you."** And the catch, which had handed a frightened reader an unreadable binary and then assumed the good half, now covers him from **John 6:37's unused second half** — *"Whoever comes to me I will never drive away. There is no screening at that door."*

**§B — `reformed-apologetics-moral-argument`: THE PAGE CONTRADICTED ITSELF THREE PARAGRAPHS APART, AND PRINTED A NOTE-TO-SELF.** Door One asserted *"No one — not Nietzsche, not the coldest materialist — actually believes that the Holocaust was merely unfashionable"*, then produced Mackie as a man who did exactly that. Resolved by conceding the error theorist exists and locating the unlivability precisely. S194's own correction had shipped its editorial trace into the public prose — *"it is worth stating plainly rather than quietly conscripting him"* — cut. *"Theism is the only position on the board"* was false (Wielenberg 2014, Enoch 2010); both are now conceded by name at full strength and the exclusivity **earned** rather than asserted (every rival must posit the fit *and then explain it*; theism has no fit to arrange). Street stated at full power including the second horn the page had skipped — the horn that matters, because **the theistic reply is itself a tracking account.** And the Euthyphro answer, which was clever but handed the atheist *parity* where premise 1 needs *asymmetry*, now turns on what kind of thing the terminus is: **obligations are second-personal** — owed *to* someone, violated *against* someone, capable of being forgiven; a brute normative fact cannot be wronged, answered to, or forgive. The emptiness charge (*"God is good" is analytic and therefore empty*) is answered for the first time: the divine nature is not **stipulated**, it is **disclosed** — *"You may look at that and conclude the standard is monstrous. What you may not say is that there is nothing there to look at."*

### Session 193 — 2026-07-28 — **THE ANONYMIZATION HELD IN THE HTML AND FAILED ON DISK, AND "FIRST MENTION GETS THE LINK" WAS NEVER ENFORCED BY ANYTHING.** Two protections that had rotted silently for months, both invisible to a validator that passed all ten checks the whole time

**THE FINDING, IN ONE SENTENCE: every check we had asked the right question about the wrong domain.** CHECK 7 asked "is this internal file blocked?" — but only of four extensions (`.md .js .txt .json`), so **27 files totalling 28 MB were being served**, among them six Netlify deploy zips, eight `.backup`/`.forge-backup` copies of live pages, four internal audit `.csv`s, `fleet-deploy.command` (which prints `/Users/aaronforman/...` in plain text), and **`RE-FORMED.pdf` — the real-name testimony**. The 2026-06-30 anonymization deleted `essays/re-formed.html` and fixed every byline (verified: "Aaron Forman" appears in **0** live HTML files) and never touched the PDF, which sat unlinked and un-sitemapped but directly reachable at `/RE-FORMED.pdf` for four months. CHECK 1 asked "does this link resolve?" — and every one of **5,047 duplicate anchors across 542 pages** resolved perfectly. **The lesson is the shape of both bugs: a check scoped to an enumerated list cannot see what nobody put on the list.** Both are now inverted to deny-by-default.

**§A — THE EXPOSURE, CLOSED AND MADE UNROTTABLE.** `RE-FORMED.pdf` and `fleet-deploy.command` removed from root; the other 25 internals swept to `archive/s193-swept/` under the forced splat. **CHECK 7 rewritten as an allowlist**: every root file is internal unless it is `.html`, `.css`, a runtime `.js` derived from actual `<script src>` tags, or named in `PUBLIC_EXACT` (Netlify control files, brand assets, `tags.json`/`testimonies.json`, the six reader-facing PDFs). It immediately caught three things the old check never could — `.DS_Store`, `.gitignore`, `.__wtest` — all now blocked, and `.DS_Store` added to `.gitignore`. **Also found: 12 rules in `_redirects` were written without the `!`** (`/.env`, `/.git/config`, the WordPress-probe traps) — un-forced rules are **shadowed by real files**, which is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md documents, so `/.git/config` was doing nothing at all. All 12 forced. **106 rules, 11 runtime assets public.**

**§B — THE HYPERLINK MANDATE, ENFORCED FOR THE FIRST TIME.** Measured in `<p>` prose with card/nav decks masked: **252 pages linked one target 4+ times, 62 pages exceeded 8**, worst `response-william-lane-craig` → `/compare-calvinism-molinism` **62 times** ("middle knowledge" linked twice in four sentences; the page reads as blue stripes). **Root cause found and fixed:** `auto-linker.js` seeded `linkedUrls` **empty on every run**, so it only ever knew what the *current* run had linked — each session's pipeline found the next still-unlinked occurrence and linked that one too, ~190 times. It now seeds from the hrefs already in the body and is **idempotent** (proven: three consecutive runs, 0 links). `dedupe-prose-links.js` written (keeps first mention, unwraps the rest, masks card decks by design) → **5,047 removed, 542 pages, 0 unique targets lost** — deduplication cannot reduce a unique-target count, so no page lost coverage. **CHECK 11 added** to fail on any prose duplicate. **Bonus catch:** the freed-up occurrences exposed a dead target in the keyword map (`/demolition-matt23-37`; real file `demolition-matthew-23-37`) which had been writing a broken link into `response-jerry-walls` — map audited (390 targets, 2 dead), fixed, and **the linker now aborts** if any `url:` has no page on disk.

### Session 191 — 2026-07-28 — **THE DETECTOR S190 BUILT WAS SCORING THE SITEMAP AND REPORTING ON THE SERMON.** On 100+ pages the "final 20%" it measured was ENTIRELY navigation cards — so `testimony-newton` sat at ZERO with the whole gospel vocabulary, hidden behind a card that said the word "substitute"; plus the fabricated author biographies that survived the S190 anonymization sweep, two hand-found feeling-slips in catches, and VOICE.md §XXIII written because the site's most-repeated defect existed nowhere in the canon

**THE FINDING, AND IT IS A LAW ABOUT MEASUREMENT.** S190's closing line was *"a detector that measures form cannot see an absent destination."* The correction is one turn further down: **a detector that measures the wrong SPAN cannot see anything at all.** `detect-gospel-absence.js` stripped the baked related-articles block and then took the last fifth of what remained — but on `demolition-romans11-32`, `testimony-spurgeon`, `devotional-the-quiet-after-the-storm` and ~100 others, what remained still ended in a `keep-reading` / `article-continue-journey` / `continue-journey-global` card grid occupying **25–30% of the body**. The window it called "the catch" was, on those pages, one hundred percent card text. It was scoring the sitemap and reporting on the sermon. Fixed in three passes: class-based **excision** (never truncation — the first attempt truncated to end-of-body and cost `philosophy-sleep-surrender` 80% of its prose, reporting a 3,505-word article as 453 words, because that page carries a journey block **mid-page**); balanced-tag matching so nested furniture comes out whole; and a second pass on **furniture HEADINGS** (`Keep Reading`, `Continue Your Study`, `Go Deeper`, `Dig Deeper`, `Where to Go Next`), because roughly a third of the corpus marks its nav block with nothing but an `<h2>`. **The corrected scan immediately surfaced a page S190 had certified at zero-absent.**

**§A — `testimony-newton` WAS ABSENT: the man who wrote "Amazing Grace," 1,792 words, no Christ.** The catch came out of the page's own material, as S190's craft law requires. ### Session 190 — 2026-07-28 — **SEVENTEEN PROSE PAGES PROVED THE DECREE AND NEVER NAMED THE SAVIOR.** Every scanner on this site was green while `analogy-river` closed on the Tao Te Ching, `demolition-hosea11-7-8` spent 2,922 words on *"How can I give you up, Ephraim?"* and never reached the One who answered it, and the HOMEPAGE ended on a lunatic scribbling darkness on a cell wall — plus the Westminster "elect infants" qualifier that `apologetic-babies` quoted and walked past, and a fabricated superlative that handed the opponent the win

**THE FINDING, AND WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT.** Session opened with all nine validator checks green, 0 structural rot, 0 broken links, canonical conformant — so the P0 audit went where tooling cannot look. A stratified cold-read (2 doorways + 4 oldest-reviewed, S58-era) returned `analogy-river` as **FAILS**, and the reason generalized: **the page contained no Christ at all.** A corpus-wide scan for the entire gospel vocabulary (*Jesus, Christ, cross, Calvary, gospel, Savior, redeem, atonement, blood, Lamb, resurrection, Messiah*) inside `<article class="article-body">`, minus the baked related-articles cards, found **17 prose pages at ZERO** and 71 more at one or two mentions across 1,300–5,500 words. **Every detector on this site measures FORM; none measured whether the page arrives anywhere.** A page can say "God" four hundred times and never reach the Redeemer — which is why bare *God/Lord/Father* are deliberately excluded from the new vocabulary: Unitarian-safe words prove nothing here.

**§A — THE 17, ALL CLEARED (ABSENT: 17 → 0).** The rule for every fix: **the catch is DERIVED FROM THE PAGE'S OWN CENTRAL IMAGE**, never a generic gospel paragraph bolted on (which would be worse than the absence). Prior version closed *"Stop fighting the banks… flow freely in the way you were always meant to go"* (Tao Te Ching ch. 8 with a veneer); also carried a **self-refuting** *"This is not poetry. This is physics"* (rivers carve — the page itself said so seven paragraphs later), a naturalistic-determinism paragraph making God one initial condition inside physics, a chess-grandmaster passage grounding the decree in **foresight (middle knowledge)**, a third analogy (fish/bowl), and a broken appositive. Fixed by *steelmanning* the carving objection and answering it (*the water deepens its bed, never reverses down; all that carving power makes the original decision more permanent*), adding the missing depravity linchpin (**every river runs down** — water has one appetite, which is what dead-in-sin means and why *"but I still choose things"* misses), and a catch on Isa 53:5: *not erosion — excavation; stone does not wear into flesh, it has to be taken out.* Close: **"He is downstream. He always was."** — the page's own *down* inverted. **`demolition-hosea11-7-8`** — the answer was hiding in its own verse 1: Hosea 11 opens *"out of Egypt I called my son,"* which **Matthew applies to Christ**; so *"How can I hand you over?"* is not a sigh but a question with an answer, and Rom 8:32 gives it in the reader's own NIV — *"gave him up for us all."* Close: **"He could not give you up. Now the qualifier is **named out loud**, what the Confession does and does not assert is stated plainly, and the hope is rebuilt on ground that holds (the Spirit "worketh when, and where, and how he pleaseth" — no reference to capacity, comprehension, decision, or age; and on any response-based theology an infant is disqualified *by definition*, so every consolation is smuggled in as an exception). **Cut the invalid argument** the page had labeled *"devastating in its simplicity"* (*if God intended to save them through hearing, He would have preserved their lives to adulthood* — excludes by assumption the alternative it must rule out, and proves too much in the mirror). **THE FIND OF THE SESSION IS A RECURRENCE OF S185'S LAW IN A SECOND SYSTEM.** S185: a classifier cannot find what its GRAMMAR never learned to name. S186 adds: **neither can a GUARD.** `auto-linker.js` protected Scripture by TAG (`<blockquote>`, `<cite>`) and, after S177/S178, by CLASS (`.scripture-text`, `.verse`, …). Both assume the verse is WRAPPED in something. **The corpus quotes Scripture inline, in ordinary prose, marked by nothing but quotation marks** — `<p>Peter writes that God is "not wanting anyone to perish…" (2 Peter 3:9).</p>` — which carries no guarded tag and no guarded class, so the linker treated the Bible as open prose and wove anchors through it. **323 INSIDE + 49 WRAPPED across 178 pages.** The fix is the same principle that fixed the sweep: quote-mark PARITY, reset at every closing block tag. `auto-linker.js` now splits text runs on quotation parity; a second run modified 0 files, and the 25 links it added later in the pipeline produced zero new injections.

**§G — A FREE-HUNT AFTER THE CLOSE ("is there anything else?") FOUND THE TWO LARGEST DEFECTS OF THE SESSION, both invisible to every existing tool because no check had ever asked their question.**

**G1 — 452 ARTICLE HEROES HAD BEEN RENDERING THEIR SUBTITLE COMPLETELY UNSTYLED.** `global.css` defines the class exactly once, as **`.hub-hero .hub-subtitle`**. Article pages use `.page-hero` and never `.hub-hero`. So on every article carrying `<p class="hub-subtitle">` — the hook line directly under the headline, the first sentence a reader meets — the CSS matched **nothing**: default body text, wrong colour, wrong size, full width, no centering, no opacity, while the 164 pages correctly using `.subtitle` got the intended ember-coloured 1.15rem treatment. **The single most-seen element on the site was broken on 74% of articles and no detector could see it, because nothing has ever checked whether a class a page uses is DEFINED FOR THE CONTEXT IT SITS IN.** Fixed by class rename on exactly the 452 pages with `page-hero` + `hub-subtitle` + no `hub-hero`; the **39 genuine hubs were identified and left untouched.** **A REGRESSION WAS INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT BY VERIFYING AFTER THE MASS EDIT:** the 15 `printable-*` pages define their OWN `.page-hero .hub-subtitle` rule inside `@media print`, so renaming the HTML orphaned their print styling; their inline selectors were updated to match. **Never assert a mass rename is done without re-grepping for the thing you renamed away from.**

**G2 — THREE META-REFRESH REDIRECT STUBS, EACH SHADOWING ITS OWN REDIRECT RULE.** `creeds-confessions.html`, `analogies-illustrations.html` and `demolition-matt23-37.html` were 5KB pages whose entire content was `<meta http-equiv="refresh">`. That is a soft redirect: slower for the reader, leaky for link equity, indexable as a thin page — **and all three were in `sitemap.xml`, so Google was being explicitly invited to index three pages that say "Redirecting…".** Worse, each was doing damage CLAUDE.md already documents: **a real file on disk SHADOWS an un-forced Netlify rule**, so `/demolition-matt23-37 → … 301` had been silently dead, `/analogies-illustrations` was a `200` rewrite serving the stub, and `/creeds-confessions` had no rule at all. **`/creeds-confessions` carried 101 inbound links** — a site-wide FOOTER nav item, 256 instances — every one of them bouncing readers through a flash. All three replaced with forced `301!`, inbound links repointed (**102 files**), stubs deleted, `HUB_REGISTRY` reassigned so `stories.html` owns the `analogy-` prefix (all 10 already wired there), and `REDIRECT_PAGES` emptied. **`canonical-conformance.js` now reports 0** — the "1 known benign flag" that rode five kickoffs was this dead redirect all along. **690 → 687 HTML.** Also found and blocked: **`_nav-template.html` was publicly served** (CHECK 7 covers internal `.md`/`.js`, not internal `.html`).

**G3 — TWO GENUINELY DIFFERENT PAGES SHIPPED THE IDENTICAL `<title>` AND `<h1>`** — `history-heresy-foreknowledge` and `history-heresy-free-will`, both "The Heresy That Won't Die." A search-result collision and a reader dead-end. Their og:/twitter: titles were **already** correctly differentiated, so only the two carriers nobody regenerates had drifted. Both now use the canonical `<h1>Title<br><span class="gold">Subtitle</span></h1>` shape.

**ALL THREE ARE NOW ENFORCED, NOT REMEMBERED.** `validate-site.js` **CHECK 8** (inline-`<style>` allowlist, all pages, warns on stale entries) and **CHECK 9** (hero-subtitle class + duplicate `<title>`) were added, on the CHECK 7 pattern that has now saved seven consecutive sessions. **The generalization, and it is the session's real lesson: EVERY ONE OF THESE WAS A RULE OR A CLASS WITH NOTHING CHECKING IT. If a documented rule has no check behind it, assume it has already rotted, and go verify it against disk.**

### Session 185 — 2026-07-21 — THE SELF-REPEATING-CLOSE DETECTOR BUILT (S184 specified it; it found 39 severe on first run), SIX LIVE FEELING-SLIPS ON PAGES `detect-feeling-slip.js` WAS REPORTING CLEAN — and the reason why: A CLASSIFIER CANNOT FIND WHAT ITS *GRAMMAR* NEVER LEARNED TO NAME

**THE FIND OF THE SESSION EXTENDS THE RECALL LAW ONE TURN.** S183 established that a classifier cannot find what its VOCABULARY never learned to name. S185 adds the harder half: **it also cannot find what its GRAMMAR never learned to name — and a vocabulary extension alone will not fix a missing shape.** Every branch of `detect-feeling-slip.js`'s TRIGGER expected the interior state as a NOUN behind a determiner (*that stirring, your ache, the flicker*). The corpus states it just as often as a **PREDICATE**, where there is no determiner to key on: *"If you are **worried** that you might not be chosen — that is evidence you are chosen"* (`the-objection-collapse`, the defect in its baldest recorded form) and *"If you are **asking** the question, you are likely in the answer"* (same tile). Adding `worried/anxious/asking/seeking/...` to `INTERIOR` changed **nothing** — the words were now known and still unreachable, because no branch could express *you are X*. A new PREDICATE branch was required. **Corpus 7 → 10 flagged; the 3 new are FPs (`response-william-lane-craig` = footer nav bleeding into a candidate sentence; `argument-if-arminianism-true-consequences` and `devotional-i-dont-think-im-saved` = "asking"/"guaranteeing" inside ordinary prose and inside a 2 Cor 1:22 quotation). The GUARD held: no token added appears in ELECT/STRONG_ELECT — `drawn` and `moved` were deliberately excluded for exactly that reason.**

**§A — `detect-self-repeating-close.js` BUILT** (specified in S184, unbuilt). Flags any ≥6-word prose span occurring in two or more separate blocks of a page; severity rises when the second landing is in the final quarter. **Two false-positive classes were found and masked during the build, and both matter:** (1) **quoted Scripture** — a verse quoted early and returned to at the close is §V.5 / Move 10, so blockquotes and every `"…"`-quoted span are masked; (2) **`div.tldr` ("In Brief")** — it EXISTS to compress the page's spine, so the body restating it is the design. That second mask alone removed the entire top of the first ranking (`systematic-tulip`'s 17-word "hit" was its own In Brief, quite correctly echoed) and cut the scored corpus 328 → 282. **Ranking is by SPAN LENGTH, not by count** — a page with one 14-word verbatim echo has the defect; a page with nine 6-word echoes is usually just carrying its central image (§IV.1). Anaphora inside a single paragraph is never flagged (§III.4 sanctions it). **Final: 282 scored / 39 SEVERE / 126 HIGH-only.**

### Session 183 — 2026-07-20 — THE `The Catch` MOLD BROKEN (34, not 21 — a colon variant no grep had ever seen), the feeling-slip detector's RECALL HOLE found and closed (v1 saw 24 pages; v2 sees the 51 it was blind to), 299 MORE hyperlinks pulled out of quoted Scripture, and `detect-ai-tells.js` BUILT

**THE FIND OF THE SESSION IS A METHOD, NOT A PAGE: A DETECTOR CAN HAVE GOOD PRECISION AND SILENTLY POOR RECALL, AND ONLY HAND-READING FINDS THAT OUT.** S182 built `detect-feeling-slip.js`, verified its precision carefully, and handed forward a 24-page queue as though that queue were the extent of the defect. It was not. The §A `The Catch` H2 sweep required reading ~34 closing sections by hand, and those sections turned out to be **the densest slip real-estate on the site** — they yielded SEVEN live slips the detector had never flagged, including **two inside PRINTABLES**, which readers hand to other people with no site around them for context. Rebuilt as v2, the detector now reports **61 pages / 75 candidates** on the pre-session corpus — i.e. **v1 was blind to 51 instances, more than double what it could see.** The standing law needs its fourth clause: a grep does not find the shape; a shape-grep does not find the direction; **and a direction-classifier does not find what its trigger vocabulary never learned to name.**

**THE THREE v1 DEFECTS, ALL REPAIRED AND DOCUMENTED IN THE HEADER.** (1) **Trigger vocabulary too narrow** — it knew "stirring / ache / leaning" but not *flicker, flinch, instinct, impulse, softening, warmth, tug*; it required "the fact that YOU" adjacently, so it missed *"the very fact that the questions made you flinch"*; it had no `your <gerund>` form, so *"Your wanting Him is evidence that He wants you"* walked through; and no adjective slot, so *"the FAINT flicker"* escaped. (2) **`DEPRAVE` fired before `ELECT`**, so a sentence merely MENTIONING resistance while claiming election was mis-filed SANCTIONED — *"if the resistance has loosened even a little — He is already prying"* is a slip wearing Move 4's vocabulary. `STRONG_ELECT` now sits between REPUDIATE and DEPRAVE; **REPUDIATE/DENIED still runs first and that order is still load-bearing.** (3) **Form 4 (CONDITIONAL COMFORT) was in the doctrine but never in the code**; now its own class, reported separately, deliberately not inflating the SLIP count. Precision was re-tightened in the same pass: bare `the answer` REMOVED from ELECT (the noise source the S182 kickoff already named on objection-love); `the call` now requires a begun/come verb; a `GOD_REF` gate added because *"evidence that the truth is true"* is not this defect however identical the grammar; and **`DENIED` now accepts possessives and appositives** — without which the detector reported **S182's own corrective lines as the defect** (*"The wanting is not YOUR proof"*, *"not a proof you were handed to audit"*). **Queue 24/30 → 7/7, all seven documented false positives (pure agency-relocation or depravity-direction).**

**TOOLING — `detect-ai-tells.js` BUILT** (specified in VOICE §XXII's tooling note, carried unbuilt since S177). **The load-bearing decision is that it has NO absolute threshold.** "Low variance" is meaningless in the abstract — a 400-word printable and a 3,000-word systematic page have different natural spreads, and any constant hard-coded today mis-scores the corpus tomorrow. So it computes the scale-free coefficient of variation for paragraph and sentence length, ranks all 656 scoreable pages, and reports the flattest tail as a **percentile against this corpus**. It earned its keep on the first run: **8 of the flattest 14 prose pages are `ethics-*`** — the same category S181 caught running an identical five-part closing machine. ### Session 182 — 2026-07-20 — THE FEELING-SLIP WAS NEVER 4 PAGES: a systemic assurance-defect found on ~25 pages (two of them inside FAQ rich-snippet JSON-LD), the "You are not holding on" family broken, and `detect-feeling-slip.js` BUILT

**THE FIND, AND IT IS THE LARGEST GUARDRAIL BREACH RECORDED HERE.** The four-form feeling-slip doctrine has ridden every kickoff since S170 as a per-page defect to hand-check. It is not per-page. It is a **corpus-wide family** — the reader's interior weather, or the bare fact that he is STILL READING, offered as EVIDENCE of his election — and it was running on roughly **25 pages** in the site's warmest, highest-traffic catch positions (consistently 61–86% of file). `detect-shared-phrases.js` surfaced the first five ("if you are reading this and something in you…"); pulling that thread unspooled the rest. **This is the site's most dangerous defect, not merely a stylistic one: a page arguing that faith is a gift, which then hands the reader a self-administered test for whether he has it, has refuted itself in its own margin — and the reader it fails is precisely the one it exists for, the man whose interior returns nothing on the day he most needs an answer.**

**WHY ELEVEN SESSIONS OF GREPS MISSED IT — the S181 law, proven a third time and now sharpened.** The slip is **grammatically identical to a SANCTIONED move**. Both say *your interior state is evidence.* They differ only in DIRECTION: interior state → evidence of **depravity** is the Corpse Inversion (§II Move 4, §XX.2) and is apex work; interior state → evidence of **election** is the slip. *"Something in you is rising to defend the story you tell about yourself"* and *"something in you is leaning toward Him — that leaning is the drawing"* are the same sentence shape and opposite theology. **No phrase-grep can separate them; only the object of the evidence-claim can.** A third class must also be spared: the **explicit repudiation**, where a page states the slip in order to deny it (invisible-wall-prayer-feels-empty's *"do not go hunting for your name in the fact that you are still reading"*; testimony-spurgeon's *"do not audit… for signs that you are one of the chosen"*). Those are models.

**FORM 3 CONFIRMED AT ITS WORST — the two most damaging instances on the site were in FAQPage JSON-LD**, i.e. the answer text Google lifts into a rich snippet, on the two pages a frightened reader is likeliest to land on. `question-am-i-chosen` ("How can I know if I am one of the elect?") answered *"that reaching is evidence the Father has drawn you… the very fact that you care is the first sign."* `question-predestined-to-hell` ("Is the fear of not being chosen itself a sign of grace?") answered *"The person who fears they are not chosen is **almost certainly chosen**."* Both re-synced to their corrected spines; all 8 JSON-LD blocks re-validated as parseable.

**~25 PAGES RE-GROUNDED, each on its own image, none rewritten to one better formula.** Highlights: **systematic-reprobation** — the fear-gauge insight (*it reads high on tender consciences and low on hardened ones, precisely backwards from what you would want a gauge to do*), then John 6:37's promise, *"whoever comes"*, with what it withholds named. **question-am-i-chosen** — *"No one has ever read his own name off the inside of his own chest"*; election is not detected by introspection but discovered by going to Christ. **ot-abel-cain** — the certificate replaced with the identical-inputs argument applied to the first two brothers (*two sons, one household, one set of inputs, different ends — name the variable*). **ot-noah** — *"Then the LORD shut him in"* substituted for *"that recognition is itself the proof."* **apologetic-no-one-can-come-unless** — the magnet kept, the self-survey killed, landing on *helkyō* as the word for hauling a loaded net (*"what it asks of the net is nothing at all"*). **systematic-regeneration** — Nicodemus's wind is *itself a denial that the thing can be tracked from inside*; *"nobody attends his own birth."* **secular-sociology-human-inability** — the literature's own finding turned on the reader's exception (*human beings are the least reliable assessors of their own condition, so an honest reader cannot use his self-assessment as the exception*). **shattered-lens-bible-doesnt-make-sense** carried form 1 AND form 2 in consecutive sentences (terror = life; *"the person who doesn't care has already lost it"*) — both repudiated in place. **demolition-matt7-7** kept its Reformed reading but relocated it from the reader's inventory to the ORDER (*"the hand that knocks is already inside the promise"*). **joy-in-suffering** now argues from desire's object rather than the reader's ache (*"no one has ever been homesick for a country that was never there"*).

**§A — THE "YOU ARE NOT HOLDING ON" FAMILY BROKEN (6 → 0).** Two were pure restatements of the sentence directly above and were **cut** (question-boasting, question-perseverance — the latter now ends on *"not at the hour of your death"*). Four rewritten onto their own images: devotional-forever-loved onto its own *chōrizō*/divorce-verb (*"A marriage is not dissolved by the doubt of one party"*), objection-faith-choice into Philippians 1:6 (*"What began without you will not end because of you"*), question-john10 onto its own hóti causation thesis, freedom onto its own whisper-in-the-dark (*"It has the wrong hand in view"*). Phrase residue **0**; the SHAPE grep confirms the surviving *"You are not X. You are Y"* instances are page-native antitheses, not the mold — though §XXII.4's *relentless antithesis* density is now worth a per-page look.

**TOOLING — `detect-feeling-slip.js` BUILT.** Classifies by the OBJECT of the evidence-claim, not the trigger phrase: **SLIP** (election) / **SANCTIONED** (depravity, Move 4) / **MODEL** (the slip repudiated). Order of tests is load-bearing — REPUDIATE/DENIED first, then DEPRAVE, then ELECT; an earlier ordering mis-filed pastoral-assurance and philosophy-infinite-regress as slips when both are correct. **It scans the whole file including JSON-LD and meta**, because that is where the worst two hid. First run: 38 pages / 47 candidates; after the fixes and the tuning, **24 pages / 30 candidates remain — the standing S183 queue**, several of which are still false positives needing further tuning.

**Also:** the S180 Scripture-link sweep missed a container class — **10 hyperlinks were still inside quoted NIV text** on printable-five-points, the-fork and testimony-wall (S180 keyed on `scripture-quote|verse-block|verse`; these sat in differently-classed `<p>` children). Unwrapped, inner text untouched. Verse-*reference* links (`passage-verse-ref`, the-golden-chain's citation label) were verified as legitimate citation labels and kept.

### Session 181 — 2026-07-20 — TWO MORE CROSS-PAGE TEMPLATES FOUND AND BROKEN (16 "Diamond" pages + a 17-page trinitarian closing machine the S180 sweep missed), the shared-phrase detector BUILT, multiplied-close 15 → 11, after-the-Amen 27 → 7

**TOOLING FIRST — `detect-shared-phrases.js` BUILT, and it found both templates in its first two runs.** Every cross-page mold broken so far (the presup trio, the testimony shelf, the Catch-Beneath H2s, the 84 Steel Man / Socratic Trap headings, the 7-page "So we confess it" machine) was found BY HAND. This finds them mechanically: n-grams of prose appearing on 3+ pages, worst-first. **The load-bearing design decision is the Scripture strip** — quoted verses are SUPPOSED to repeat verbatim across pages, and the first run returned nothing but John 6:44 on 74 pages and Ephesians 2:8-9 on 53. Container-stripping is not enough because most verses sit *inline in prose inside quotation marks*; the fix is to drop every quoted span before n-gramming. Flags: `--n` (gram length), `--min` (page threshold), `--tail` (closing 25% only — the highest-signal mode, since closing machines are the loudest tell). ### Session 179 — 2026-07-20 — PROSE WORK LOST to API failures (0 pages edited) — but the site's INTERNAL STRATEGY DOCS were found PUBLICLY SERVED and blocked, and the close detector's false-positive root cause was found and FIXED (queue 60 → 48; no page needs a manual skip any more)

**No HTML page was edited this session.** The multiplied-close queue is exactly where S178 left it. Stated plainly so no future agent re-derives work that was never done.

**FAILURE FIRST — three cold-read agents, three API deaths.** Three parallel `general-purpose` agents were launched with **3 full HTML pages each**; all three died to API 529 / mid-response server errors after burning 27K / 91K / 99K subagent tokens, two of them seconds from returning. **`SendMessage` is not exposed in this harness, so there is no resume path and the work was unrecoverable.** **The lead's own error, and the more important one: the detector was not run BEFORE delegating.** `node detect-multiplied-close.js <page>` prints the labelled beats in ~15 lines and costs almost nothing; run afterwards, it disqualified 3 of the 6 pages outright. **STANDING RULE: profile with the detector before launching any burst; 2 pages per agent, never 3.**

**CRITICAL — INTERNAL STRATEGY DOCUMENTS WERE BEING SERVED PUBLICLY. NOW BLOCKED.** Verified live over HTTP, not inferred: `https://adoptedbygrace.net/CLAUDE.md` and `https://adoptedbygrace.net/VOICE.md` both returned in full, `Content-Type: text/markdown` (VOICE.md = 644 lines, the complete style bible). There is no `netlify.toml`, `.gitignore` does not exclude `.md`, and Netlify publishes the repo root — so **all 148 root-level `.md` files were reachable**: the manifesto, the style bible (including §II "The Twelve Lethal Moves" and §XXII's "I don't want anyone who reads this website to know an artificial intelligence wrote it"), MISSION-CONTROL and its archive, SAPIENTIAL-AUDIT, and 120 session kickoffs. Note this is not a §XXII.6 honesty breach — the site has never denied authorship — but the *playbook* being one URL away, in the least charitable possible vocabulary, is a serious and asymmetric exposure. **THE FIRST FIX SILENTLY FAILED, AND THE REASON IS THE LESSON.** An enumerated `410` rule was added for all 148 root `.md` files ahead of the catch-all — and `https://adoptedbygrace.net/VOICE.md` still returned 644 lines after deploy. **Netlify redirect rules are SHADOWED by real files: if a file exists at the requested path, Netlify serves the file and IGNORES the rule unless the status is FORCED with a trailing `!`.** The pre-existing rules in `_redirects` (`/.git/config`, `/backend/.env`) only ever worked because those paths do not exist on disk. Never again assert a redirect fix without re-fetching the live URL. **THE SHIPPED DESIGN (Aaron chose zero-build):** (1) the root-pinned docs that tooling loads by path — `CLAUDE.md`, `VOICE.md`, `MISSION-CONTROL*`, `SAPIENTIAL-AUDIT*` — each carry a **forced** `410!` rule; (2) **everything else internal moves under `archive/`**, covered forever by the single forced splat `/archive/*  /404.html  410!` — 119 session kickoffs moved, and 43 internal audit `.txt` reports staged into `archive/reports/`; (3) four audit `.json` files pinned individually. The 151-line enumerated block was deleted: it went stale the moment files moved and gave false confidence. **A build-time strip via `netlify.toml` was written and verified (194 `.md` + 43 `.txt` stripped, robots/tags.json/PDFs surviving) and then DELIBERATELY REJECTED** — `package.json` carries `netlify-cli` + `jsdom`, so any build command triggers dependency installation and converts a free static deploy into a real build, against the standing "every deploy costs build minutes" rule. `netlify.toml` now exists solely to document that decision and warn the next agent off re-adding one. **The habit the design depends on is now CLAUDE.md INTEGRITY LAW 6: new internal documents go in `archive/`, never the repo root.** Also swept: a **second exposure class missed on the first pass** — 43 internal audit `.txt` reports (`CONTENT-AUDIT`, `BROKEN-LINKS-SCAN-RESULTS`, `SEO-AUDIT`, the tier3 buckets) were being served as `text/plain`. `robots.txt` and the site-verification token were verified and kept. **THIRD AND FOURTH EXPOSURE CLASSES, swept in the same pass:** all **55 build-only `.js` scripts** (the site loads only 11; `detect-multiplied-close.js` and `auto-linker.js` describe the site's own machinery in their header comments, which is the strongest remaining §XXII.3 tell in the repo) plus `package.json`/`package-lock.json`, and **27 further root working documents** including `system-prompt-snapshot-2026-04-22.md`. **THE PROTECTION IS NOW ENFORCED, NOT REMEMBERED — `validate-site.js` CHECK 7.** It derives the runtime allowlist from the actual `<script src>` tags in the HTML (so a genuine new front-end script needs no edit) and FAILS the validator if any internal root `.md`/`.js`/`.txt`/`.json` lacks a forced rule, printing the exact line to add. Negative-tested: removing the `/VOICE.md` rule exits 1 and names the file; restoring it exits 0. **CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION: Aaron verified `/VOICE.md` and `/auto-linker.js` both return 404 after deploy.** `_redirects` now carries **94 unique forced rules + the `/archive/*` splat**, deduplicated (a one-group `re.findall` bug had produced 67 duplicate lines mid-session, caught and rebuilt).

**TOOLING — `detect-multiplied-close.js`: ONE root cause behind ALL THREE false-positive classes, now fixed.** S178 recorded the-two-arms (16) and objection-why-believe (14) as permanent manual skips caused by "grid `→ THEN →` connectors." **That diagnosis was wrong.** The real bug: the block regex `<(p|blockquote|div|h2|h3)\b…>([\s\S]*?)<\/\1>` treats `<div>` as a leaf while not tracking nesting, so a structural wrapper captures only up to its FIRST child's `</div>`, collapses to two or three words, and scores as a `hammer`. Fixes applied: **(1)** a container-`<div>` skip (a div wrapping any block-level child is furniture; its real prose children are still matched on their own pass); **(2)** the "Go Deeper" / "Explore Further" rail stripped surgically in BOTH its `<section>` and `<div>` forms — its inline-styled card blurbs were the actual source of objection-why-believe's score; **(3)** diagram/equation classes added to the furniture list (`chain-node` etc. are leaf divs whose only child is a `<br>`, invisible to the container test; `math-*` likewise); **(4)** legal/utility pages (`terms`, `privacy`, `404`) excluded — `terms.html` had been ranking in the worst 32. **Results: the-two-arms 16 → 1 · objection-why-believe 14 → 0 · the-golden-chain 6 → 3 · devotional-when-god-says-no 8 → 5 (cleared). Site-wide 2 severe + 60 multiplied → 1 severe + 48. The "skip these two pages" instruction carried in every kickoff since S178 is now OBSOLETE — delete it.** **One self-inflicted regression, caught and reverted:** adding `<section class="chain-link-scene"` as a truncation marker cut the-golden-chain to **zero** blocks, because that marker sits at **9%** of the body — precisely the trap the file's own header comment documents. Truncation markers were verified empirically (`further-reading` earliest at 63%) and then rejected anyway in favour of surgical stripping, since `twoarms-math` is *followed* by the page's real close.

**Also:** the two stale web-root artifacts `index.html.orig` and `question-freewill.html.bak` are blocked from serving; the sandbox denied `rm`, so their deletion is folded into the push command. **120 stale `NEXT-SESSION-S*-kickoff.md` files** sit in the repo root (S68 → S180) — now unserved, but clutter awaiting Aaron's call on archiving.
